title: About
body:
The e-commerce landscape has evolved significantly over the past two decades, driven by advancements in technology and changing consumer behaviors. A comprehensive understanding of the customer journey is essential for any business operating in this space, particularly for American multinational companies that focus on e-commerce. This journey can be segmented into three primary phases: pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase.

During the pre-purchase phase, potential customers engage in information gathering and evaluation of options. Research indicates that approximately 81% of shoppers conduct online research before making a purchase decision. This phase is critical as it sets the foundation for customer expectations and influences their eventual purchasing behavior. Companies must ensure that their online presence is optimized for search engines and that they provide valuable content that addresses customer needs and concerns.

The purchase phase is where the actual transaction occurs. This phase is characterized by the importance of user experience, as studies show that 70% of consumers abandon their shopping carts due to poor website functionality or complicated checkout processes. Therefore, it is imperative for e-commerce businesses to streamline their purchasing processes, ensuring that they are intuitive and efficient. Additionally, offering multiple payment options can enhance customer satisfaction and reduce cart abandonment rates.

Following the purchase, the post-purchase phase plays a crucial role in customer retention and brand loyalty. Research indicates that acquiring a new customer can cost five times more than retaining an existing one. Therefore, businesses should focus on providing excellent customer service, facilitating easy returns, and engaging customers through follow-up communications. This phase can significantly influence repeat purchases and customer referrals, which are vital for long-term success in the e-commerce sector.

In conclusion, understanding the e-commerce customer journey is essential for companies aiming to thrive in a competitive market. By focusing on each phase—pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase—businesses can enhance customer satisfaction, improve conversion rates, and foster brand loyalty. As the e-commerce industry continues to grow, companies must adapt their strategies to meet the evolving needs of consumers, ensuring a seamless and positive experience throughout the entire customer journey.

Electric Bikes

Electric bikes — commonly known as e-bikes — are bicycles fitted with a battery-powered motor that assists your pedalling, making hills easier, commutes faster, and longer rides more accessible than ever. Whether you're looking to ditch the car, explore off-road trails, or simply enjoy cycling without the strain, there's an electric bike built for you.

Types of Electric Bikes

  • Electric Cargo Bikes
  • Electric City Bikes
  • Electric Fat Bikes
  • Electric Folding Bikes
  • Electric Mountain Bikes

Why Buy an Electric Bike From Us?

We carry a curated range of e-bikes across every riding style — from cargo bikes built to haul the family to lightweight folders for the daily commute — so you're comparing real options, not settling for whatever's in stock. Every bike ships backed by manufacturer warranty coverage, and our team is on hand before and after your purchase to help you pick the right motor, battery range, and frame size for how you actually ride.

  • Fast, reliable shipping
  • Hassle-free returns
  • Manufacturer warranty on every bike
  • Flexible financing options available
  • Real riders on staff for sizing and fit questions

Electric Bike FAQs

[accordion: How far can an electric bike go on one charge?]

Most e-bikes travel roughly 20 to 60 miles per charge. Battery size, assist level, rider weight, terrain, and tire pressure all change the real number, so check the range listed on each bike's page.

[/accordion]

[accordion: What are Class 1, 2, and 3 e-bikes?]

In the US, Class 1 bikes assist only while you pedal, up to 20 mph. Class 2 adds a throttle, also up to 20 mph. Class 3 assists while you pedal up to 28 mph. Where each class is allowed depends on your local rules.

[/accordion]

[accordion: Do I need a licence or insurance to ride one?]

Rules vary by country, state, and class. Many places treat Class 1 and 2 e-bikes like regular bicycles, but check your local regulations before you ride.

[/accordion]

[accordion: Which type of e-bike is right for me?]

Commuters usually like city bikes, small spaces suit folding bikes, trails call for mountain bikes, and hauling kids or cargo is what cargo bikes are for.

[/accordion]

title: Electric Skateboards - After-item lists
body:
Electric Skateboards

Types of Electric Skateboards

  • Mini Boards – Short, lightweight boards (usually under 11 kg) designed for shorter trips and easy portability. Often feature a detachable battery pack under 99 Wh that is airline-safe.
  • Street Boards / Flexy Boards – Relatively lightweight boards with flexible decks and smaller street wheels (under 115 mm). Most use a two-piece battery and ESC enclosure for better flex and average range (similar to the original Boosted Board).
  • AT (All-Terrain) / 2-in-1 Boards – Hybrid boards with larger wheels (115 mm+), a single-piece battery/ESC enclosure, and carbon-fiber or wooden decks. Suitable for city streets plus light off-road use like grass and gravel; typically dual belt-drive motors.
  • Off-Roaders – Larger, heavier boards based on mountain-board decks. Built for rough terrain and steep hills with dual (or sometimes quad) motors, top-mounted battery boxes for ground clearance, and optional suspension, bindings, or mudguards.
  • Racing Boards – High-performance boards with low, stiff decks and wide rubber wheels. Often feature 3-link trucks for stability at speed and powerful ESCs (sometimes over 15 kW peak). Usually rear dual-motor setups used in racing events.

title: FAQs - ace-p-51-electric-bike
body:
Is the P-51 Ace street legal?

Yes. The Ace is a Class 2 e-bike, which legally qualifies it as a bicycle — it can go almost anywhere a bicycle is allowed. No license is required, but riders should follow local laws.

What is the max weight for a rider?

We recommend no more than 275 lbs.

What if I'm tall (6'2"+)?

A 3-inch riser bar or our Stem Riser gives taller riders a more comfortable, upright position.

What's the range of the Ace on a single charge?

Approximately 40+ miles on throttle only, varying with terrain, rider weight, and riding style.

How long does it take to charge the battery?

About 3 hours for a full charge from empty, using the included 5A quick charger. Partial charges take less time.

How does the pedal-assist system work?

The motor adds power as you pedal across levels 1–5. Level 0 lets you ride on throttle alone with no pedal assist.

Can I ride the Ace without using the electric assist?

Yes — it pedals like a traditional bike with or without assist engaged. Full-sized crank arms give a bigger range of motion when pedaling.

Is the Ace suitable for off-roading or trail riding?

Yes. With its off-road tires and full suspension, the Ace is built to handle trails and off-road terrain comfortably.

How durable is the Ace's frame?

The Ace uses a rugged aluminum frame with a forged head tube for added strength, built for durability while keeping the bike light and agile.

What safety features are integrated into the Ace?

Hydraulic brakes, responsive handling, and integrated head and tail lights for visibility. The tail lights include running lights and brighten further when braking.

How do I turn on the headlight?

Press and hold the + button on the left side panel to turn on the headlight and rear running lights.

Are you currently shipping outside the US?

Not yet — stay tuned for updates.

Are you offering test rides?

Yes, at our showroom in Huntington Beach, California.

Are replacement parts available for maintenance?

Yes, we offer a range of replacement parts for maintenance and repairs. Reach out to our team with any questions.

How do I maintain the battery for longevity?

Avoid extreme temperatures, charge regularly, and store at around 50% charge if the bike won't be used for an extended period.

Can I use the Ace for daily commuting?

Yes — it's well suited for quick, eco-friendly daily commuting around your city or town.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this ebike waterproof?

This ebike is not fully waterproof, but it is built to an IPX5 water-resistant standard, meaning it's protected against low-pressure water jets from any direction. This makes it safe to ride in light to moderate rain or through small puddles. Avoid full submersion, and never use a pressure washer or high-pressure sprayer to clean it.

Do you sell a conversion kit for this model?

No, we don't sell conversion kits. Every bike we make comes with its own integrated battery, motor, and sensors, engineered together as a complete system for the best riding experience.

How do I maintain my ebike battery?

To extend your ebike battery's lifespan, follow these battery care steps: charge it regularly without letting it fully drain, use only the correct charger on a flat non-flammable surface, avoid overcharging, and store it in a climate-controlled space away from extreme heat or cold. For long-term storage, keep the battery at around 75% charge, avoid exceeding the bike's max load rating, and keep the battery, terminals, and ports clean.

What accessories are included with my ebike?

Some models include pre-installed fenders and a rear rack out of the box. Additional accessories — including helmets, locks, and bike pumps — are available separately in our accessories collection.

What warranty comes with the bike?

All frames, framesets, components, and batteries are covered by a 2-year warranty. See full warranty terms.

What maintenance does an electric bike need?

Electric bikes need regular maintenance tune-ups, similar to traditional bikes or cars. Check tires, tubes, chains, battery, and brakes regularly, or visit a local bike shop for professional service. Performing a pre-ride safety check and staying current on non-electric component maintenance also helps extend the bike's life.

title: off-road-electric-scooters
body:
Off-Road Electric Scooters

Explore off-road electric scooters built for riders who want more capability beyond ordinary city streets and paved bike paths. These all-terrain electric scooters combine powerful motors, rugged construction, capable tires, suspension systems, strong braking, and extended-range batteries to handle a wider variety of riding conditions, from gravel roads and dirt paths to grass, trails, hills, and rough pavement.

Whether you're looking for a dual-motor off-road electric scooter, a fast performance scooter for challenging terrain, a long-range all-terrain scooter for outdoor adventures, or a comfortable electric scooter for mixed-surface riding, this collection brings together models designed for demanding recreational and outdoor use.

What Makes an Electric Scooter Off-Road?

An off-road electric scooter is designed with features that improve traction, stability, comfort, durability, and performance beyond smooth paved surfaces. Compared with lightweight commuter scooters, off-road models commonly emphasize motor power, torque, suspension, tire traction, ground clearance, braking performance, battery capacity, and frame durability.

Key Features

  • Dual motors: Can provide increased traction, acceleration, and hill-climbing capability.
  • All-terrain tires: Larger pneumatic, tubeless, or treaded tires can improve traction and stability on loose or uneven surfaces.
  • Suspension: Front, rear, or full suspension can help absorb impacts and improve comfort.
  • Powerful motors: Higher-output motors can provide stronger acceleration and torque for hills and demanding terrain.
  • Large batteries: Higher-capacity batteries can provide greater potential range for longer rides.
  • Strong brakes: Performance-oriented braking systems provide controlled stopping on heavier or faster scooters.
  • Durable construction: Rugged frames and components can better withstand vibration and demanding riding conditions.
  • Ground clearance: Additional clearance can help when traveling over uneven surfaces and obstacles.
All-Terrain Electric Scooters for Different Riding Conditions

"Off-road" can describe many different riding environments. A scooter that performs well on gravel and packed dirt may not be appropriate for deep mud, loose sand, steep technical trails, or extreme terrain. Always match the scooter to the conditions you actually intend to ride.

Gravel, Dirt, and Trails

Gravel and dirt can reduce traction and make steering less predictable. All-terrain tires, suspension, adequate ground clearance, and appropriate motor power can help provide a more controlled ride on loose or uneven surfaces.

Grass and Mixed Surfaces

Grass can introduce additional rolling resistance and reduced traction, particularly when wet. Scooters with suitable tires and sufficient torque can be better suited to mixed surfaces than lightweight commuter models.

Hills and Inclines

Hill-climbing performance depends on motor configuration, torque, battery voltage, rider weight, incline, tire traction, terrain, and battery state. Dual-motor electric scooters are often considered by riders who prioritize stronger traction and hill performance.

Rough Pavement

Off-road capability isn't limited to dirt trails. Cracked pavement, uneven roads, rough sidewalks, and poorly maintained surfaces can also make larger tires and suspension valuable.

How to Choose an Off-Road Electric Scooter

The best off-road electric scooter depends on your terrain, riding experience, performance requirements, range expectations, and budget. Start with where you plan to ride, then compare the specifications that matter most for that environment.

  1. Identify your terrain. Consider whether you'll primarily ride pavement, gravel, dirt, grass, trails, hills, or a combination of surfaces.
  2. Choose the motor configuration. Determine whether a single motor provides enough performance or whether a dual-motor scooter better fits your riding conditions.
  3. Compare tires. Look at tire diameter, width, tread pattern, construction, and recommended pressure.
  4. Evaluate suspension. Front, rear, or full suspension may be preferable depending on how rough your riding environment is.
  5. Consider battery and range. Compare battery capacity and expected real-world conditions rather than relying exclusively on advertised maximum range.
  6. Check braking performance. Heavier and faster scooters benefit from braking systems appropriate for their weight and performance.
  7. Check rider capacity. Make sure your weight and riding equipment fall within the manufacturer's specified limits.
  8. Consider scooter weight. High-performance off-road scooters can be substantially heavier than commuter scooters and may be difficult to carry or transport.
  9. Review intended use. Choose a model whose manufacturer specifically supports the type of terrain and riding conditions you intend to use it for.
Off-Road Electric Scooter FAQs

What is an off-road electric scooter?

An off-road electric scooter is designed with features intended to improve performance and stability beyond smooth pavement. Common characteristics include larger or treaded tires, suspension, stronger motors, durable construction, increased ground clearance, and performance-oriented braking systems.

Can electric scooters go off road?

Some electric scooters are specifically designed for off-road or all-terrain riding, while many commuter scooters are intended primarily for paved surfaces. Always check the manufacturer's intended-use recommendations before riding on dirt, gravel, trails, or other uneven terrain.

Are dual-motor electric scooters better for off-road riding?

Dual-motor scooters can provide advantages in traction, acceleration, and hill climbing. However, they can also be heavier and consume more energy than many single-motor models, so the best configuration depends on your terrain and intended use.

What tires are best for off-road electric scooters?

The appropriate tire depends on the terrain. Wider pneumatic, tubeless, or treaded all-terrain tires can provide useful traction and cushioning on many loose or uneven surfaces, while smoother tires may be more efficient on pavement.

Are off-road electric scooters good for commuting?

Some off-road scooters can work well for mixed commuting and recreational riding, particularly when routes include rough pavement or unpaved sections. However, they are often heavier and less portable than dedicated commuter scooters.

What should I look for in an off-road electric scooter?

Pay particular attention to motor configuration and torque, tire size and tread, suspension, braking, battery capacity, ground clearance, rider weight capacity, scooter weight, water resistance, and the manufacturer's intended riding conditions.

title: Lectric XPeak2 Step-Thru eBike - FAQs
body:
xIs the XPeak2 Step-Thru a Class 1, 2, or 3 electric bike?

The XPeak2 can be ridden as a Class 1, 2, or 3 e-bike, giving you the flexibility to match local e-bike laws. In Class 3 mode, pedal-assist tops out at 28 mph. No license or registration is required, but riders should always check state and local regulations.

Is the XPeak2 a good off-road electric bike?

Yes. As a purpose-built off-road electric bike, the XPeak2 pairs an 80mm-travel RST Renegade suspension fork with puncture-resistant 26" x 4" fat tires, so it handles trails, gravel, sand, and uneven terrain with confidence.

What makes the XPeak2 a fat tire electric bike?

The XPeak2 rolls on 26" x 4" knobby fat tires designed for extra traction and stability across mixed and off-road terrain. Like all our fat tire electric bikes, they come Slime-filled at no added cost to help prevent flats.

What is the range of the XPeak2 Step-Thru on a single charge?

The XPeak2's electric bike range is up to 60 miles per charge in pedal-assist mode, depending on rider weight, terrain, and assist level used. A full charge takes 6–8 hours with the included charger, or about 4 hours with the optional 5A Fast Charger.

What kind of electric bike battery does the XPeak2 use?

The XPeak2 runs on a removable 48V, 15Ah (720Wh) lithium-ion electric bike battery certified to UL 2271, semi-integrated into the down tube for a clean look and easy access.

How does the pedal assist on the XPeak2 work?

The XPeak2 is a pedal assist electric bike that uses a PAS torque sensor with PWR+ technology, which reads your pedaling effort and delivers smooth, natural-feeling power across five assist levels. A thumb throttle is also included if you'd rather ride without pedaling.

Can I ride the XPeak2 as an electric mountain bike?

Yes. The XPeak2 is built and eMTB safety tested to ISO 4210-10, making it a capable electric mountain bike for trail riding, with a hydroformed aluminum frame, suspension fork, and hydraulic disc brakes rated for off-road use.

What's the payload capacity and max rider weight?

The XPeak2 has a payload capacity of up to 330 lbs, including a max rider weight of 330 lbs and a max rear rack load of 60 lbs. Always distribute weight within these guidelines for safe handling.

How long does it take to assemble the XPeak2?

Most riders can assemble the XPeak2 in under 5 minutes — simply attach the quick-release pedals, install the front wheel via the thru axle, and secure the handlebars with 4 screws. No special tools required.

What braking system does the XPeak2 use?

Hydraulic mineral oil disc brakes with a 203mm front rotor and 180mm rear rotor deliver strong, reliable stopping power in wet or dry conditions.

Is the XPeak2 Step-Thru good for shorter or less mobile riders?

Yes — the low-standover Step-Thru frame (19.5" stand-over height) makes it easy to mount and dismount, and the telescoping, adjustable seat post fits riders roughly 5'2" to 6'3".

How do I maintain the XPeak2's battery for the long term?

Avoid extreme heat or cold, charge it regularly rather than letting it fully drain, and if you're storing the bike for an extended period, keep the battery at around 50% charge.
